title: Between F and 2F: the projector
caption: For f = 10 cm an object at 15 cm (between F and 2F) gives a real, inverted image at 30 cm, magnified 2×. Moving the object to 12 cm pushes the image to 60 cm and 5×. A projector puts the slide just beyond F: for a screen 5 m away, 1/u = 1/10 − 1/500 gives u = 10.2 cm, magnification 49.
alt: Two ray diagrams for a converging lens of focal length 10 cm: an object at 15 cm forms a real inverted image 30 cm away, twice the size; an object at 12 cm forms one 60 cm away, five times the size.
description: Each panel shows a converging lens of focal length 10 cm with F and 2F marked, and the three ray rules for an object between F and 2F.
Object at 15 cm: 1/v = 1/10 − 1/15, so v = 30 cm; the image is real, inverted and 2 times the object's height.
Object at 12 cm: v = 60 cm and the image is 5 times as tall.
The closer the object is to F, the farther away and larger the image: the lesson's projector has u = 10.2 cm and v = 500 cm, magnification 49.
